evals.prompt: We're doing a full rebrand — new name, new logo, new everything. Can you design and build our new homepage?
evals.expected_output: Should run the front-door diagnosis, identify this as a Revolution, and refuse to build a site on an undefined system — routing back to creative-direction (and brand-strategy if the emotional target isn't set) before any design work. Should hold that position even if the user says they already have a logo, since a mark without the system around it isn't enough for a coherent site. Should note that a missing .agents/design.md is itself the 'go back' signal.
assertions: Runs the front-door diagnosis and classifies as Revolution
Routes back to creative-direction rather than designing
Holds the position even when a logo already exists
Treats missing .agents/design.md as the go-back signal

evals.prompt: Here's our brand guide and design.md. Build the homepage — just use placeholder copy for now and we'll fill in the words later.
evals.expected_output: Should refuse to build around placeholder copy: the site is built around the words, never the reverse, and wireframe-first thinking is the fastest tell of an assembled page. Should route to the marketing library's copywriting / website-copy (or ask for the real copy) first, explaining that the designer's job is to give what's being said its proper emphasis. Should also note headline scale follows the actual content rather than a fixed hero shell.
assertions: Refuses placeholder/filler copy as the basis for the design
Routes to copywriting / website-copy or asks for the real copy first
Explains copy-first: design gives the message proper emphasis
Notes size/scale follows the content, not a template

evals.prompt: Redesign this page to look better: https://example.com — our brand is settled and design.md is up to date.
evals.expected_output: Should proceed (settled brand = Optimization) but insist on faithful replication: inventory the source top to bottom and port every section with the right copy and order, reproduce the primary action mechanism (not just its words), and pull the real partner/integration logos rather than icon-plus-text stand-ins. Should ship real custom code in the project's stack (or clean HTML/CSS), not a mockup or a Webflow/Framer build. Should apply the system from design.md rather than inventing alongside it — including one reserved forward CTA color used only on actual CTAs, and rhythm as a vocabulary of varied section types rather than one repeated card idiom.
assertions: Proceeds because the brand is settled (Optimization)
Inventories and ports every section, preserving the primary action
Pulls real logos, not icon+text stand-ins
Ships real custom code, not a comp or platform build
Applies design.md's system; CTA color reserved for actual CTAs only
Varies section types/media rather than repeating one layout idiom

evals.prompt: The build looks good. Now make it feel alive — add a bunch of animations, including a big scroll-telling section where the heading pins.
evals.expected_output: Should take the motion character from the brand's emotional target rather than a generic default (playful vs. premium produce different motion; 'slick' is not the universal goal). Should split the work: build the functional/UI floor here — named easing with ease-out as the workhorse (no raw linear), UI transitions under ~300ms, press feedback, entrances that overlap and stagger rather than queue, transform/opacity only, hierarchical (not uniform) reveals, and prefers-reduced-motion honored — while handing the expressive pinned scroll-telling choreography to motion-design. Should recommend GSAP (ScrollTrigger) for the pinned sequence rather than hand-rolling it, while keeping CSS for simple states. Should push back on 'a bunch of animations' as uniform fade-up slop and validate by watching the rendered page, not screenshots.
assertions: Derives motion character from the brand, not a house default
Builds the functional motion floor inline (ease-out, <300ms, transform/opacity, reduced-motion)
Uses overlapping/staggered entrances rather than sequential queuing
Hands the pinned scroll-telling sequence to motion-design
Recommends GSAP/ScrollTrigger for the complex sequence, CSS for simple states
Pushes back on uniform 'animate everything' as slop; validates by watching the page

evals.prompt: You've rebuilt https://example.com in our stack from design.md. I scrolled through it and it looks right — same hero, same vibe, same CTA. Can we call it done and ship? (The source has nine sections; the build has eight. The 'use it anywhere' surfaces section between features and pricing was never ported.)
evals.expected_output: Should not accept 'looks right at a glance' as done. Should run the match loop from faithful-replication: grade a source-specific checklist against side-by-side screenshots of the source and the build at 1440px and 390px, never from memory. The measured section-count-and-order check should catch the gap — nine sections on the source, eight on the build — name the missing 'use it anywhere' section and where it belongs (between features and pricing), and grade that line 'no'. Should port the section with its real copy, re-screenshot both widths, and regrade the full checklist. Should also check hero proportions against a stated tolerance. Should stop after two rounds and hand off for human review with the graded checklist and screenshots rather than declaring it shipped.
assertions: Refuses to sign off on a glance; runs the match loop instead
Screenshots source and build at 1440 and 390px and grades against them, not memory
Section count/order check catches the dropped section (9 vs 8) and names it
Ports the missing section in the right position, then re-screenshots and regrades
Checks hero proportions against a stated tolerance
Stops after round 2 and hands off for human review with the graded checklist and screenshots

evals.prompt: Finish the site and ship it. Give me the accessibility report too. (The build's mobile menu toggle is an icon-only <button> containing an SVG, with no aria-label or visible text. Nobody has tested the page with a screen reader.)
evals.expected_output: Should run the accessibility report from references/accessibility-report.md on the rendered page and report every item as Passed, Issue found, Needs manual testing, or N/A. Should catch the icon-only menu button with no accessible name, report it as Issue found, and state the fix (e.g. add aria-label="Open menu" and toggle aria-expanded) — then apply it and re-test before changing its state. Should report screen-reader flow as Needs manual testing, noting what was checked in the accessibility tree and what a human should listen for. Should never mark Passed anything it could not fully test — items it could only partly verify (e.g. text contrast over imagery) are Needs manual testing, not Passed. Should not declare the site 'accessible' or 'compliant' as a blanket verdict, and should point to web-design-guidelines for the full compliance pass.
assertions: Reports each checklist item as Passed, Issue found, Needs manual testing, or N/A
Reports the unlabeled icon-only menu button as Issue found, with a concrete fix (accessible name via aria-label or visible text)
Reports screen-reader flow as Needs manual testing
Marks nothing Passed that it could not fully test; unverified or partly verified items are Needs manual testing
Makes no blanket 'accessible' or 'compliant' claim
Points to web-design-guidelines for the full interface/accessibility compliance pass

evals.prompt: Homepage is done. The FAQ accordion and the mobile menu are just divs with onClick handlers and some aria attributes I added — they open and close fine. Can we ship?
evals.expected_output: Should block the ship: hand-rolled ARIA on divs is not an accepted build for interactive pieces. Should rebuild both on a tested headless behavior library — staying with shadcn/Radix if the project already uses it, otherwise Radix, React Aria, or Base UI. Should then verify on the rendered page by tabbing through both pieces: the accordion is reachable and operable from the keyboard, the mobile menu closes on both Escape and outside click, and focus returns to the menu trigger on close rather than dropping to the body or page top. 'Opens and closes fine' with a mouse is not a pass.
assertions: Refuses to ship the hand-rolled div accordion and menu
Rebuilds both on a headless behavior library (stays with shadcn/Radix if present; otherwise Radix, React Aria, or Base UI)
Tabs through both pieces on the rendered page rather than trusting mouse testing
Confirms Escape and outside click both dismiss the mobile menu
Confirms focus returns to the menu trigger after it closes

evals.expected_output: Should design a hero that gives the headline commanding scale rather than trapping a half-width H1 in a 50/50 split beside a media box, and should not put a row of three or four stats along the bottom of the hero. Below the hero, the type scale should use three or fewer body sizes (hero display type and the nav wordmark don't count), with subheads set apart by weight and color rather than extra 20–24px steps. The hero should have one primary CTA — not a button wall, and not an automatic secondary link just to fill the template.
assertions: Does not use a half-width H1 with a stat row (the 50/50 template hero)
Uses three or fewer body sizes below the hero
Has one primary CTA
